xray.one_line: A travel platform that runs AI agents for travellers (trip planning, support, voice, car rental) and for its partner properties (guest messaging).
xray.what_it_does: Booking.com, part of Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: BKNG), is an online travel platform connecting travellers with accommodation, flights and car rentals. Since June 2023 it has added generative AI across the booking journey: the AI Trip Planner (built on its own recommendation models and partly on OpenAI's ChatGPT API), Smart Filter and Property Q&A, and from October 2025 its first in-house agentic tools, Smart Messenger and Auto-Reply for partners, alongside AI Trip Support, AI Voice Support and an AI Car Rental Helper for travellers. It also runs an app inside ChatGPT for browsing stays and rental cars, which hands the traveller back to Booking.com to book. [s1, s3, s4, s5]

situations.title: Smart Messenger answers a property's guests
reach: Partner, property and reservation information, which Smart Messenger gathers to decide what to suggest or do
Guests: suggested replies and instant Auto-Reply answers go to travellers in the partner-to-guest messaging channel
The partner's Extranet inbox, where Smart Messenger, Auto-Reply and Help Me Reply are live
Past interactions and user feedback, from which the agent keeps learning and adapting its responses
Payment requests in the same channel: compromised partner accounts have used Booking.com's official guest messaging to ask guests for card details, with real booking information
asked_our_example: Suggest replies about the property and the stay; the partner approves each one before it is sent
Answer instantly only on the topics the partner has defined in Auto-Reply
Never ask a guest for payment or card details in a message
gap: Booking.com says Smart Messenger gathers information to autonomously take action; public material does not say which actions it takes without the partner's approval.
The agent writes in the channel that phishing has used to request card details from guests; no public description says how agent messages about payment are limited or marked.
Learning from past interactions: what is kept, and whether it is scoped to one property, is not publicly documented.

situations.title: A traveller cancels a stay by phone with AI Voice Support
reach: The caller's booking details, which the tool pulls once connected
Trip management, including cancellation requests; Booking Holdings' CEO says Booking.com customers can now cancel bookings through agentic AI
Property information used to answer questions and support reservation changes (AI Trip Support)
Human customer service agents, who receive the case with all necessary information on handover
asked_our_example: Act only on the caller's own reservation, after the caller is matched to it
Cancel only after reading back the cancellation terms and getting a clear yes
Hand to a human for anything outside the property's policy
gap: Public material does not say how a caller is matched to a booking before the tool pulls booking details.
Whether the tool completes a cancellation itself or hands it to a person, and what confirmation it asks for, is not publicly documented.

situations.title: Planning a trip and booking from the AI Trip Planner
reach: Booking.com's recommendation models and accommodation inventory
Booking.com pricing shown with deep links to property details
The traveller's past searches and travel history when signed in
The in-app accommodation booking flow: one tap on a property to complete the reservation
OpenAI's ChatGPT API, which partly powers the conversation
asked_our_example: Recommend and show options; a booking happens only when the traveller taps through and confirms
Use account history only to personalise this traveller's results
gap: Which parts of the conversation and account history reach the third-party model is not publicly documented.
Booking.com's chief business officer named wrong prices and irrelevant content as the failure mode; prices shown in chat are a path to a booking.

questions: Smart Messenger gathers information to autonomously take action: which actions can it take without the partner approving them, and can a partner require approval for every message?
Guest messaging has been used to phish guests for card details: can Smart Messenger or Auto-Reply ever send or suggest a payment request, and is such a message marked or held?
How is a caller matched to a reservation before AI Voice Support pulls booking details, and does it complete a cancellation itself or hand it to a person?
Which traveller data (conversation, account history, reservation details) is sent to third-party model providers, and is each agent action recorded against the booking it touched?
Press reports an internal agent platform with guardrails for prompt injection and personal data: will Booking.com publish what those guardrails cover for the agents that touch reservations?
incidents: 2023-09: Phishing through Booking.com's guest messaging: attackers took over hotels' Booking.com accounts, extracted guest booking data and messaged guests demanding card details to avoid cancellation. Booking.com said its backend was not breached and described new measures to lock or block inactive partner extranet accounts. The same channel is where Smart Messenger and Auto-Reply now operate; the incidents did not involve the AI agents. [s18, s17]

2026-03: Reports continue of compromised hotel extranet accounts used to send fraudulent payment requests through the official guest messaging system (not involving its AI agents: the same messaging channel the Smart Messenger agent now uses) [s19]

help.label: Our hypothesis, not their claim. Built from public pages only; nothing of theirs was tested.
help.pitch: RiskMandate would measure, for one real deployment of Booking.com's agents, what each agent was asked to do (its mandate), what its credentials and connections actually let it reach (its grant), and the difference between the two (the gap), and keep that as a written record. It is read-only: never in the request path.
